title: Stream API: source, intermediate and terminal operations

videos.script: A stream is a description of work on a sequence of values. It is not a collection, and the difference is the whole lesson. {{loop}} Here is a loop that finds the titles of cheap books, and here is the same question as a stream: a source, two steps, and an end. {{lazy}} Now watch what happens when the end is taken away. The steps print nothing at all. A stream does no work until a terminal operation asks for a result. {{order}} And when it does work, it does not finish one step for every book before starting the next. Each book goes through all the steps, one at a time, and the stream stops as soon as it has what it needs. {{once}} Last, a stream can be used once. Ask it twice and Java says so.
